intro: The accepted Reserve chapters 4–5 and their seven-beat plan remain unchanged. These additions finish the surrounding cash-flow and life-event chapters. Record each segment separately; the reusable explanation is prepared, while exact screens and outcomes require the approved build.

beats.rehearse: Start from W01's original cash flow, not the reduced-spending state. Reveal income, tax-payment provision, living costs, required debt and employee contribution one row at a time. Employer match is additional retirement money.
beats.say: Before assigning the next dollar, check what has already come out. The amount left should be something we can follow back to the records.
beats.verify: Actual gross/net income mapping, business-payment treatment, tax payments versus liability, source freshness and household contribution totals. A real engine tax result is not forced to match the illustrative $4,000 provision.
beats.finish: Explain the original $500 remaining amount or reconcile the actual modeled difference without invented balancing entries.

beats.rehearse: Review the available spending period and one annual cost, one one-time cost, a credit-card settlement/transfer, and an uncertain transaction. Compare a representative estimate with the actual bill/payday cycle.
beats.say: An unusual month can distort the average, but an annual bill still needs money. Let's decide which costs the future plan should carry.
beats.verify: Supported source coverage and spending-method choices; actual exclusion and correction receipts. No simulated transaction feed or unsupported category control.
beats.finish: Record the chosen spending basis, what it includes, and one specific uncertainty to resolve.

beats.rehearse: Preview the $1,200 living-cost reduction: $10,800 to $9,600; $500 to $1,700 remaining after the employee contribution. Identify the real cancellations, negotiations or habit changes required before adoption.
beats.say: This larger amount depends on a change. We haven't found extra money in the original budget. Here is what the household would have to do to make it real.
beats.verify: Current versus proposed amounts, effective date, save/reload and resulting Plan freshness. Exact category reductions require the fictional capture extension; do not fabricate their provenance.
beats.finish: The original and reduced states are separately named, and the outside spending action remains honest.

beats.rehearse: Enter one expected vehicle need and income change using the reviewed fictional dates and amounts. Compare a possible renovation separately. Follow purchase price, financing, payment and funding through the affected year, then rehearse the event becoming actual.
beats.say: The event needs an amount, a date and a funding source. When it happens, the real records and future entry need to tell the same story once.
beats.verify: Life-event ownership, recurrence, current/future-dollar units, associated debt, preview/save and planned-to-actual handling. No invented vehicle quote, date or automatic lifecycle behavior.
beats.finish: The expected event has a clear funding explanation, while the unchosen renovation remains a what-if.

beats.rehearse: Use $58,000 education resources assigned $29,000 per child. For the oldest, $20,000 for four years leaves $51,000 over 60 months, or the labeled $850 flat-cost zero-growth benchmark. Put it beside the already fully routed reduced cash flow.
beats.say: The benchmark tells us the scale of the gap. It doesn't create another eight hundred fifty dollars. We need to change a commitment, a funding source, or the timing.
beats.verify: Actual account owner/beneficiary and access; supported event/account attribution and funding calculation. External benchmark stays separate from an app result. No use of the same education money twice.
beats.finish: Choose an affordable plan or name the unresolved trade-off; no college obligation is added for a member it does not apply to.

intro: Use the same debts entered in W01 and the named reduced-spending comparison from W02. The Reserve decision and Austin's liquidity judgment carry through this session; no new lender application or actual loan is authorized.

beats.rehearse: Review each existing obligation's balance, required payment, rate, collateral and maturity. Identify variable, interest-only and guarantee terms. Distinguish an unused line from borrowed money.
beats.say: The payment is what the household has to support now. These terms tell us what could change it.
beats.verify: Exact editable debt fields and save/reload; unsupported contract clauses remain in the reviewed operating sheet, not imagined controls.
beats.finish: Required payments and the obligation most exposed to an income interruption are clear.

beats.rehearse: Show DTI beside actual cash flow, then included gross assets and current/stressed DTA. The partial stress holds the HSA/education values unchanged and omits unvalued business/vehicle assets. Explain a loan-specific LTV separately.
beats.say: The household ratio and the lender's collateral ratio answer different questions. A house on the balance sheet may not meet a rapid collateral call.
beats.verify: Source denominator, actual supported stress output and contractual thresholds. Clearly label separate teaching arithmetic rather than forge an app stress report.
beats.finish: Member can distinguish payment capacity, household leverage and collateral pressure.

beats.rehearse: Assign debt jobs and the reduced-state $1,200 extra card payment while preserving $500 Reserve funding. Add the separate verbal single-income/dependent variation without changing the Reed fixture.
beats.say: Faster debt reduction saves interest, but it uses cash now. When essential bills would otherwise depend on more borrowing, the household may need to build accessible cash faster.
beats.verify: Required versus extra payment fields, actual interest/amortization assumptions and payoff result. No invented payoff date or reclassification of the Reeds as single income.
beats.finish: Each debt has an action, reason and review trigger, and all amounts fit the same available pool.

beats.rehearse: Compare the same $30,000 project and date using cash, an eligible taxable sale and a faithfully modeled financing alternative. Cash from $32,000 Reserve leaves $2,000. Include smaller/delay and compare additional Bitcoin separately.
beats.say: Financing keeps cash at the start, but the payment still needs room. This phase already uses the available surplus. What actually changes to make the project affordable?
beats.verify: Loan fees, rate schedule, principal exit, collateral and tax funding. Label unsupported HEI/balloon/business terms in an external reviewed schedule. Keep the $20,000 loan arithmetic illustration separate.
beats.finish: Adopt no proposal without explaining cash remaining, new payments, total obligation and fallback. Delay is a valid decision.

beats.rehearse: Complete purpose, repayment, maturity, personal review level, lender action level, maximum additional collateral, operator and backup. Test an unavailable refinance and a fast decline.
beats.say: The rules need to tell us what to do before the lender has to act. Another loan is a possibility, not a guaranteed repayment source.
beats.verify: Actual agreement, notice/discretion and modeled fields. Monitoring and alerts do not guarantee time to respond or prevent liquidation.
beats.finish: The household can explain a usable response without pledging every remaining asset by default.

beats.rehearse: Return to Cash Flow and reconcile $775 employee + $500 Reserve + $1,200 extra debt = $2,475 before employee contributions. Explain the future $1,605 released only after actual card payoff.
beats.say: This debt decision uses the same money we just reviewed. The later contribution plan begins only when that obligation has really ended.
beats.verify: The same canonical extra-payment decision appears once and reloads correctly; future start/stop controls or outside reminder are truthfully identified.
beats.finish: W04 receives the final affordable current claim and separately labeled future routing conditions.

intro: Record each allocation decision together with the relevant account and cash-flow facts. Current holdings, target, contributions and actual trades are separate. Keep the source categories and unavailable exact investment menu honest.

beats.rehearse: Read one portfolio by asset, use date, account treatment and actual holding. Reconcile the $1,307,000 teaching subset with the app's actual eligible denominator.
beats.say: These are four views of the same money. Before comparing percentages, check that the same assets are included.
beats.verify: Included/excluded accounts, asset classification, pledged/restricted money and no duplicated totals.
beats.finish: Name one actual mismatch in access, holding or intended use before choosing a change.

beats.rehearse: Compare Current with the hypothetical 60/34/6 target. Show the $509,600 isolated Bitcoin stress loss and the household funding implications; other assets can decline too.
beats.say: A target is supportable when the household can carry its obligations through the difficult case. It is not automatically a trade we should place today.
beats.verify: Same scope, real comparison/save semantics and any actually modeled effect; the separate stress illustration is not an engine result.
beats.finish: Record the target, reason, downside and what would prompt review.

beats.rehearse: Inspect current needs, early-access years, later years and dedicated events. Keep Reserve/Bridge/Forever investment horizons separate from account-access dates, with both spouses' timelines.
beats.say: When will we use this money, and can this account provide it then? Those are two questions to answer before routing more into it.
beats.verify: Supported account assignments, access conditions and year funding; do not invent event-to-account attribution.
beats.finish: Identify the first real funding gap and the accounts that can address it.

beats.rehearse: Show all current claims fitting the one pool, with employer $387.50 separate. Current additional investment is zero; later $1,605 is conditional on card payoff and an updated cash-flow check.
beats.say: This phase uses the money available. A later contribution needs a later source, not another row claiming the same surplus.
beats.verify: Actual current/future routing controls, start dates and save/readback. Unsupported conditional automation remains a dated outside task.
beats.finish: Explain where a new available dollar goes today and what event changes the answer.

beats.rehearse: Compare only accounts relevant to the identified job. Check access, eligibility, cost and the investment menu. Show a menu item as unknown until verified in the fictional capture extension.
beats.say: The account earns its place by doing a job. We do not need every account type from the example.
beats.verify: Owner, tax type, provider/plan availability and account-opening status; no fictional label establishes an actually available fund.
beats.finish: Each contribution has a usable account or a specific unresolved eligibility/menu task.

beats.rehearse: Use the equal-pretax Traditional/Roth arithmetic graphic, then compare the actual modeled current election, Roth or split under reviewed tax inputs. Read take-home-pay consequences.
beats.say: Compare the same economic budget. A change that costs cash today still needs to fit with the Reserve and debt decisions.
beats.verify: Current election not inferred from account label; actual tax calculation and qualified/access conditions; payroll execution separate.
beats.finish: Record the intended tax election or focused professional question, not an invented permanent winner.

beats.rehearse: Review the different account mixes and combined target. Show the $56,200 target gap as direction, not a trade. Compare the future $1,000 personal Bitcoin/$605 taxable stocks route only in its conditional phase.
beats.say: The account tells us where money lands. The investment election tells us what it buys. Different account mixes can support the same household target.
beats.verify: Supported current/asset-class/specific-holding routing, security identities, tax/access effects and actual available cash.
beats.finish: Every contribution has an amount, account, tax treatment and intended holding; the combined total remains coherent.

beats.rehearse: Build the short outside action list: payroll, transfer, account opening, fund-menu verification or recurring purchase. Give each an owner and date.
beats.say: This is what the plan records, and this is what still has to happen with payroll or the provider.
beats.verify: Saved versus Preview state and relevant receipts. No executed trade, loan or automatic bank transfer is claimed.
beats.finish: All current claims fit, accounts are usable, holdings support the jobs, and implementation status is honest.

intro: Use synthetic purchase records and a separately reviewed tax-year scenario. Record calculations as calculations and professional/transaction work as pending until actually performed. Do not publish private tax files.

beats.rehearse: Read the three-lot table for the same 0.2 BTC sale and $20,000 proceeds. Compare $8,400/$16,800/$9,600 gains with their allocated bases.
beats.say: The cash received is the same. The cost of the units identified for sale changes the gain. Now check which units and identification process the records actually support.
beats.verify: Known quantity, basis, date/holding period, fee convention, current identification rules and applicable custody location. No legal conclusion from an app ordering setting.
beats.finish: Distinguish proceeds from taxable gain and name any evidence needed before a sale.

beats.rehearse: Upload one accepted source example, review an overlap, a transfer and a missing purchase detail. Compare the current position before and after adding evidence.
beats.say: History explains what is already here. It should not add the same Bitcoin twice or turn an unknown purchase into a known zero cost.
beats.verify: Certified adapter or supported guided mapping, reconciliation and actual receipt; no sale/repurchase substitutes or universal source-coverage claim.
beats.finish: Current holdings stay nonduplicative and missing facts have a prioritized evidence task.

beats.rehearse: Read employment, lower-income years, benefits and later required distributions. Compare income types rather than treating all spending proceeds as income.
beats.say: This is the period worth investigating. What else uses the same tax room, and which decision should we compare?
beats.verify: Actual tax roadmap, jurisdiction/year, relevant account access, separate withholding and liability.
beats.finish: One specific tax-window comparison is identified with its unresolved facts.

beats.rehearse: Compare Current with a bounded conversion and an accessible spending withdrawal where relevant. Show conversion money, tax-payment source and household spending separately, then after-tax resources at matching future dates.
beats.say: This money moved into Roth treatment. It does not also pay the bills. The additional tax uses a separate resource, so read that cost with the future benefit.
beats.verify: Real incremental tax, liquidity, opportunity cost, healthcare/RMD effects only as modeled; label external review. No invented Reed conversion result.
beats.finish: Choose a comparison to pursue, reduce or reject; planned and actual conversions remain distinct.

beats.rehearse: Evaluate one gain/loss-harvesting candidate or deliberately pass. Prepare identification, replacement exposure, current income and deadline checks before any actual transaction.
beats.say: We have a possible opportunity. Verification, outside execution and recording are separate stages.
beats.verify: Actual year and asset rules, costs, carryforward evidence and custodian process. A proposed action is never displayed as executed.
beats.finish: The candidate has prerequisites and a next step, or a documented reason to pass.

beats.rehearse: Produce the supported FORM 8949 TAX DATA CSV, inspect coverage and package the relevant records, assumptions and exact CPA question.
beats.say: This is data for review and filing preparation. It is not the filed return, and a successful export does not prove every record is complete.
beats.verify: Actual export schema, values, gaps and safe handling; no file sent or professional approval claimed.
beats.finish: The packet supports one useful professional conversation and preserves next-year continuity.

intro: The retirement example requires completed, reviewed capture inputs and the actual approved model. Keep the $108,000/$40,000/$68,000 arithmetic illustration distinct from adopted spending, benefits and final withdrawals. Record no favorable ending in advance.

beats.rehearse: Read the first retirement year and a year when income changes. Separate lifestyle, healthcare, tax, debt and events from reliable income and portfolio funding.
beats.say: Follow what comes in and what has to go out. The rough gap is the starting calculation; this is the full cash need and how it is funded.
beats.verify: Gross/net units, income dates by person, spending inclusion and actual year detail/result identity.
beats.finish: Explain why the draw differs across the important years without duplicated costs.

beats.rehearse: Map both adults' early years to actually usable accounts and later benefits. Compare the funding cost of waiting for a benefit with the later income where relevant.
beats.say: Enough total wealth is not the same as enough usable money in this year. Point to the actual account and the access condition.
beats.verify: Reviewed account/age/separation/ordering rules and real benefit inputs; no assumption every account unlocks at 59½ or every benefit should start at one age.
beats.finish: Every bridge year has a credible path or a specific access/funding decision still open.

beats.rehearse: Compare realistic coverage paths with normal- and high-cost-year exposure. Connect the same income assumptions to tax and coverage costs and each spouse's transition date.
beats.say: A lower monthly premium is only part of the choice. Read the coverage and retained risk, then check whether this tax decision changes the net cost.
beats.verify: Current quotes or clearly hypothetical inputs, eligibility/enrollment and any externally calculated assistance; no fabricated subsidy engine or medical anecdote.
beats.finish: The planning cost and dates match a path to verify before current coverage ends.

beats.rehearse: Compare strict account order and one intentional blend, then asset-sale priority. Inspect immediate cash and later distribution years using unchanged spending and market assumptions.
beats.say: First choose the account, then what is sold inside it. Follow the tax funding before calling the withdrawal spendable cash.
beats.verify: Actual cash gross-up, conversion separation, lot support and access. No claim the engine automatically finds the optimal blend.
beats.finish: Member can explain the next withdrawal, sale and tax source as one coherent funding choice.

beats.rehearse: Use the existing exact sequence graphic, then inspect actual reserve target, sources, refill and a weak-market year near the floor.
beats.say: Cash gives us time. If the weak market lasts, we still need a response before the cash no longer covers the bills.
beats.verify: Actual modeled reserve/refill rules and nonduplicative transfers; unsupported desired rules remain a recording hold, not a simulated feature.
beats.finish: Name use/refill/floor responses and the resources supporting them.

beats.rehearse: Compare the same retirement cash need using sales, another account and a supported borrowing policy. Read strategy, assumptions and difficult-year debt/collateral/interest/repayment.
beats.say: Keeping more Bitcoin initially is one benefit. Here is the additional obligation and what would repay it when conditions are worse.
beats.verify: Rate-over-time, collateral exposure, capitalized interest, eventual exit and current/hypothetical/actual-loan separation. The 50% input default is not safe or recommended. No invented liquidation or provider-failure frequency.
beats.finish: Choose the understood policy and state risks the model does not quantify.

beats.rehearse: Compare one realistic spending/timing/funding change and inspect the year that explains its effect. A preferred date below the standard is an acceptable actual teaching outcome.
beats.say: What changed, what did it do, and what did the household give up? A better percentage alone does not settle the decision.
beats.verify: Same input set, percent/count/horizon, current result and changed assumptions; no target score produced through hidden changes.
beats.finish: Member can explain the preferred comparison and its trade-off.

beats.rehearse: Read standing portfolio guardrails separately from an annual spending proposal. Connect inflation, annual change limit and reserve funding, then complete the retirement operating summary.
beats.say: This portfolio level prompts a review. This separate amount is the spending change we are considering, with its limit and funding effect.
beats.verify: Validated inverse thresholds and denominator; actual policy, capped change, annual state, save/reload and exceptions. Never repeated-save to evade the cap or relabel percentages as dollars.
beats.finish: The chosen next-year spending, income, portfolio sources, reserve policy, borrowing rules and review date tell the same story.

intro: Use the named Family Custody Map and its filled fictional example. The planning record contains no signing secrets and never certifies an unperformed or unrelated recovery test.

beats.rehearse: Complete one row for direct custody, one professional pool and one brokerage-fund exposure. Compare job, control, support and dependency.
beats.say: Each method solves a different part of the household's needs. Name the protection it gains and the risk it still keeps.
beats.verify: Actual supported Protect fields and source account identities; methods are not ranked by wealth or assumed secure by brand.
beats.finish: Every meaningful pool has an intentional direction and one next protection action.

beats.rehearse: Read D07's actual test receipt and its scope. Separate practice-wallet recovery from a check relevant to an existing funded wallet.
beats.say: This is what the test proved on this setup. It does not prove a different wallet's backup works.
beats.verify: Correct wallet/setup, actual safe test and remaining unknowns. Do not mark the real holding recovered just because a practice balance appeared.
beats.finish: Tested versus pending status accurately identifies the relevant method and evidence.

beats.rehearse: Identify a shared email/phone, provider or operator failure. Choose one external hardening action and safely show its actual confirmation or leave it pending.
beats.say: A second login doesn't help if the same failure blocks both recovery routes. Fix the dependency we actually found.
beats.verify: Actual provider controls, safe recovery alternatives and evidence; no passwords or usable recovery codes in footage.
beats.finish: One material improvement has an owner and honest completion status.

beats.rehearse: Record the non-secret first contact, review triggers and outside tasks. Match the Family Custody Map to the supported planning status and distinguish app backup from wallet backup.
beats.say: The family needs a safe place to start. The financial plan does not need the information that can move the Bitcoin.
beats.verify: Real export/restore behavior separately; no descriptors, xpubs, exact recovery locations or full signing route added.
beats.finish: The map is usable, the dependencies are named and recovery status is truthful.

intro: Use the actual blank and fictional Heir Letter, Executor Packet, Family Custody Map and insurance audit. These coordinate decisions; they are not legal documents or professional approvals.

beats.rehearse: Separate incapacity and death roles, primary/backup willingness, document status and institutional beneficiaries.
beats.say: This is who is intended to help, and this is the authority or process that still needs to be confirmed.
beats.verify: Supported non-secret fields, attorney review and nomination versus appointment; no checkbox creates legal authority.
beats.finish: Each role/document gap has a focused professional or family next action.

beats.rehearse: Connect one direct-custody row and one institutional row to the legal owner, authorized role and operational helper. Test the unavailable-operator case.
beats.say: Being able to move an asset and being entitled to act are different. We need a process that respects both.
beats.verify: Actual agreement and lawful provider process; no universal seed/passphrase split or owner impersonation.
beats.finish: Each important pool has a legitimate starting path and named unresolved questions.

beats.rehearse: Fill the Heir Letter's first page and the Executor Packet's coordination index. Ask a consented nontechnical listener for the first action and how to verify the contact.
beats.say: The letter gets you started; the packet organizes the follow-up. Let's check whether the first step is clear without my explanation.
beats.verify: Real harmless delivery, opening and comprehension; no claimed listener test before execution and no signing material in the packet.
beats.finish: Revise the actual confusing passage and record the true test result.

beats.rehearse: Demonstrate the communication backstop only after verifying it in the actual release/account mode. Use an explicitly authorized harmless recipient and message.
beats.say: This delivers direction, not keys. A missed check-in and a message arriving are separate things to test.
beats.verify: Recipient, waiting period, false-alarm/cancel path, delivery and access; no assumed 90-day default or delivery guarantee. Missing promised capability remains held and reported.
beats.finish: Document the tested route and a fallback not dependent on the unavailable person's login.

beats.rehearse: Complete one material risk in the insurance audit using actual policy mechanics or a clearly hypothetical example. Compare need with cap, waiting period, exclusions and retained risk.
beats.say: We are deciding which loss the household can carry and which needs coverage or further review—not buying one of every policy.
beats.verify: Licensed review, private contract evidence and replacement effective date; no invented app insurance-analysis feature.
beats.finish: Each material risk is checked, intentionally retained, or assigned a specific review.

intro: Use the same household and the Annual Plan Refresh. Keep monthly facts, annual strategy and urgent exceptions as distinct review tasks.

beats.rehearse: Time an actually quiet check: current accounts, cash flow, reserve transfer, upcoming events and result freshness. Stop with zero to three useful actions.
beats.say: We are checking what changed. A quiet month does not need a new allocation or an invented task.
beats.verify: Actual source state and timing; do not promise every review takes five minutes.
beats.finish: Member can repeat the brief check and knows when to stop.

beats.rehearse: Resolve one synthetic discrepancy at its source. Compare resolved, deferred, snoozed and uncertain states and the effect on the current position.
beats.say: Find the reason for the difference before creating a record. A postponed question is still open.
beats.verify: Supported recovery action and receipt; no fabricated transaction or cash balance to force agreement.
beats.finish: The material issue is resolved or assigned with its consequence clear.

beats.rehearse: Open the prior dated plan and complete Annual Plan Refresh across position, cash flow, debt, allocation, tax, retirement and protection. Revisit the actual card-payoff and reserve milestones before re-routing money.
beats.say: These choices affect each other. A payment ending creates room to reconsider, not an automatic claim that the money is free for another purpose.
beats.verify: Current data, supported comparison and annual-spending state; tax deadlines and collateral/security monitoring retain separate cadence.
beats.finish: The annual record explains what changed, why, and which outside actions remain.

beats.rehearse: Adopt one reviewed fictional income/event change, then compare a strategy response separately. Check immediate essential cash needs before long-term optimization.
beats.say: This is the fact that changed. This is the response we're considering. Keeping them separate lets us understand the new result.
beats.verify: Actual save/update/freshness, event lifecycle and unchanged hypothetical/actual distinctions; no invented Recalculate control.
beats.finish: The baseline reflects the new fact and the chosen response is explicit.

beats.rehearse: Save the dated readable plan, annual record and action list; identify the separate protected backup and next monthly/annual/urgent review triggers.
beats.say: Next year's review starts here, with the decisions and reasons intact. The backup has a different job from the readable summary.
beats.verify: Actual export and tested restoration capability; no calendar event, outside message or completed task claimed just from writing a reminder.
beats.finish: The household has a repeatable review path and an honest dated record.

intro: The capstone must reconcile to one actual saved fictional plan, not a composite of different teaching phases. The prepared documents and arithmetic do not substitute for the engine-backed plan and listener test.

beats.rehearse: Read the actual report beside Household Plan Summary: current position, current cash flow phase, contribution claims, intended/calculated timing, assumptions and risk.
beats.say: Every statement in this summary should describe the same plan. Let's trace the important numbers back to their sources.
beats.verify: Actual report, source rows and calculation identity; no original/reduced/post-card state mixing or landing-page placeholder results.
beats.finish: The summary and report explain the same facts and choices.

beats.rehearse: Inspect first retirement, benefit start, a major event and a later tax-sensitive year. Follow spending, tax, withdrawals, debt and ending resources.
beats.say: These are the years when funding changes. The headline makes more sense when we see where the money comes from here.
beats.verify: Real outputs from the same accepted inputs; unknowns remain visible, no fabricated favorable finish.
beats.finish: Member can explain the meaningful transitions and the most important limitation.

beats.rehearse: Give the short household explanation to a consented nontechnical listener and ask for the next cash source and first safe absence-response action.
beats.say: You don't need every technical detail. Tell me where next month's money comes from and who you would contact first.
beats.verify: Actual listener understanding and corrections; no private client footage or assumed successful pilot.
beats.finish: Revise the explanation where the listener cannot follow it, and record what actually happened.

beats.rehearse: Prepare focused CPA, attorney, insurance or lending handoffs using the relevant documents, evidence and one concrete question each.
beats.say: This packet gets the professional to the decision that needs review. Preparing it does not mean they have approved it.
beats.verify: Supported exports, private evidence handling and genuine open questions; no message sent or professional appointment/approval claimed.
beats.finish: Each consequential unresolved issue has the correct evidence and next recipient/action.

beats.rehearse: Save the dated readable plan, Household Plan Summary, next priorities, Annual Plan Refresh starting point and separately verified protected backup.
beats.say: These are the next priorities, not a claim that only three tasks remain. The plan is useful when the decisions and unfinished work are clear.
beats.verify: Save/reload/export/restore scope and actual remaining approvals; no publication or full course-completion claim from files alone.
beats.finish: The member can explain and maintain the plan; final capture and pilot evidence are separately recorded.

intro: This is a separately approved, small-value test demonstration. Record the exact hardware, firmware, wallet software, backup standard, official procedure/date and review before filming. No test is authorized on the household's only working funded device.

beats.rehearse: Verify device source and authenticity, create the isolated test wallet and explain PIN, backup and any passphrase. Keep secret generation and backup out of captured footage entirely rather than rely on later blurring alone.
beats.say: This is a practice setup. We are checking which information it needs and what a successful recovery would prove.
beats.verify: Exact current manufacturer instructions and complete recovery requirements. Prewritten recovery words or unexpected screens mean stop.
beats.finish: Only the documented non-secret setup is shown, with validated backup steps identified before any destructive action.

beats.rehearse: Receive a trivial authorized test amount through the trusted address check. Use the supported non-destructive backup check or compatible spare recovery first. Reset/restore only when explicitly part of the reviewed test procedure.
beats.say: Check the backup before risking the working setup. We need to recover this intended test wallet, not merely open an empty wallet that looks valid.
beats.verify: Expected wallet/test balance and exact passphrase/configuration requirements. A mismatch is an abort: do not reset the source device, add meaningful funds or mark recovery complete while troubleshooting.
beats.finish: The actual intended test wallet is recovered under the reviewed procedure, or the test remains failed/pending with a safe next step.

beats.rehearse: Verify a small outbound test and fee, then write what the demonstration proved and what remains untested. Review all distributable footage for secrets and unnecessary identifiers.
beats.say: This proves the procedure on this test setup. It does not prove the backup of a different funded wallet. That holding needs its own safe, relevant verification.
beats.verify: Transaction confirmation, test scope, no usable keys/configuration in exported footage, and separate actual-holding recovery status. No universal fee/dust threshold or provider endorsement.
beats.finish: W07 receives an accurately scoped receipt; the actual household recovery status is not overstated.
